title: KL10/PDP-10 primary and secondary engineering documents

records.title: DECsystem-10/DECSYSTEM-20 Processor Reference Manual
records.use: First source for programmer-visible PDP-10/KL10 instruction and system-operation semantics. Chapter 3 is especially important for KL10 paging, PI/APR and RH20 behavior.

records.title: KL10 Technical Reference Manual
records.use: Hardware-level reference. The manual describes KL10-R systems as having at least 512K words of memory except the 1091, making it the primary source for the minimum-memory question in the current boot work.

records.title: Extended Addressing on the DECSYSTEM-20: Programming Implications and Methodology
records.author: Dan Murphy
records.use: Primary explanation of Model-B extended effective-address computation and section-aware control flow. Use whenever execution leaves section zero.

records.title: DEC STD 159 Massbus Specification
records.use: Bus-level reference for Massbus details that are below the processor programmer model.

records.title: KL10 Model-B production microcode preservation / emulator repository
records.use: Contains the recovered final TOPS-20-capable KL10 Model-B microcode and source-level organization. Use for exact micro-sequencing questions after establishing the architectural contract.

records.title: KL10 production BLT microcode
records.use: Use for BLT normal-copy versus clear-core paths, parity wait, and restart/fixup sequencing.

records.title: Richard Cornwell PDP-10 KL/KI/KS CPU implementation
records.use: Practical secondary reference for how another emulator implements KL10 behavior. Verify important semantics against DEC documentation or microcode before adopting.

records.title: Richard Cornwell RH10/RH20 interface implementation
records.use: Useful secondary implementation model for channel transfer and NXM completion/status behavior.

records.title: Richard Cornwell DF10 common channel implementation
records.use: Shows explicit DMA memory-boundary checks and channel completion on nonexistent memory; useful when auditing our channel paths.
